title: First Law of Thermodynamics
notes: - The first law is conservation of energy for a thermodynamic system: ΔU = Q − W when W is the work done by the system.
- Q is heat added to the system. If the system does work, W is positive in this sign convention, and internal energy falls unless heat is supplied.
- Internal energy U is a state function, so ΔU depends only on the initial and final states. Heat and work depend on the path taken between those states.
- In a cyclic process the system returns to its start, so ΔU = 0 and Q = W: the net heat absorbed equals the net work done by the system.
- An isolated system has Q = 0 and W = 0, so ΔU = 0. A machine that produces work with no energy input contradicts this law.

The first law says the rise in internal energy equals the heat added to the system plus the work done on the system. A common school form writes ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW with ΔW the work done by the gas. The two forms agree if you keep the sign of W consistent. This note uses work done on the gas.
